text:
For a **longer outage**, look for a portable power station with **about 2,000 Wh capacity**, a **pure-sine-wave AC outlet**, and enough continuous output for your heater and thermostat. Capacity is the key: a 24 W heat mat might run roughly **1½–2 days** on a 2 kWh station after inverter losses and the station’s own power use; a 100 W ceramic heat emitter cycling at half power might run about **a day**. Treat those as estimates, not guaranteed runtimes. ([runtime estimates](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage), [sizing guidance](https://offgridpowerboom.com/reptile-heat-battery-backup/))

For a **short outage**, a smaller station may do; for overnight or multi-day backup, aim for more capacity. Check the heater’s wattage label and the station’s continuous-output rating, and keep the heater on its reptile thermostat. During a brief outage, insulating the enclosure can help conserve heat too. ([Petco outage guidance](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage))

If you share the heater’s wattage and how many hours of backup you want, I can estimate the capacity you need more closely.
